chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

The diyah is one thousand dinars or ten thousand dirhams. And from the people who possess garments, garments are taken; from the people who possess camels, camels are taken; from the people who possess sheep, sheep are taken; and from the people who possess cattle, cattle are taken.

key_terms.أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ: one thousand dinars as a stated valuation of the diyah
key_terms.اَلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due in cases of unlawful killing or bodily injury
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: ten thousand dirhams as an alternative stated valuation of the diyah
key_terms.ٱلْإِبِلِ: camels used here as a compensatory asset category
key_terms.ٱلْبَقَرِ: cattle used here as a compensatory asset category
key_terms.ٱلْحُلَلِ: garments or suits of clothing accepted here as a compensatory asset category
key_terms.ٱلْغَنَمِ: sheep used here as a compensatory asset category

ai.seo_question: What is the amount of diyah, and in what forms may it be paid according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed amount of diyah and indicates that compensation may be taken according to the wealth form commonly possessed by the liable party. It reflects a legal framework in which financial liability is assessed through recognized monetary standards and transferable property categories.
